title: ASSAY: browser dashboards for the EI LLM, Page Code and HELM, tested end-to-end on real Qwen and DeepSeek repositories (pre-registered BEFORE running)
naming: The browser-run EI LLM is named ASSAY. An assay determines what a sample ACTUALLY contains, independently of what its label claims -- which is precisely the stack's founding rule F_out = F_eval. The name is a verb as well as a noun ('assay this claim'), it is short enough for a browser tab, and it is not a generic AI product name.
what_the_novora_stack_is_for: The stack solves ONE problem: you cannot tell whether a piece of software, a model, or a claim is trustworthy by looking at how popular it is. Every component exists to measure verified behaviour instead of reported reputation -- NERE/IHCEI gates the reasoning, PAGES scores text and ABSTAINS when there is no signal instead of bluffing, Page Code decides what an agent is permitted to change, Echo writes every verdict into a tamper-evident hash chain, EI ties them together and must expand the human's options rather than replace their judgement, and the Agency allocator spends limited repair budget on the weakest link first.
cohort: 22 REAL open-source repositories fetched live from the GitHub REST API on 2026-08-06: 10 from org QwenLM (Alibaba) and 12 from org deepseek-ai, all with stars > 500, frozen to ei-dashboards/data/qwen_deepseek_frozen.json. Fields are real: stars, forks, open_issues, license (SPDX id or null), created, pushed, archived, language, description, topics.
honest_data_note: The Hugging Face MCP connector dropped mid-session, so this cohort is GitHub-only and was NOT supplemented with a fresh Hugging Face pull. Qwen models DO appear in previously frozen HF fixtures (hf-cohort 3 entries, hf-media 1 entry) and those are cited as-is; no new HF data is claimed. Nothing is fabricated to fill the gap.
components_under_test: Every gate below calls the REAL committed stack module -- not a reimplementation: novora-suite/engine/fastmode.mjs (screen), page-code/pagecode.mjs (auditChange, CodePermissionTable), echo/echo.mjs (EchoDB, merkleRoot, verifyInclusion), ei/ei.mjs (EI.evaluate, EI.verify), and agency-constitution/constitution.py (ConstitutionalAllocator).

gates.D1_pages_abstains_not_bluffs: NOVORA PAGES. Run screen() over the real repository descriptions. A repository whose description is EMPTY must produce an abstain verdict ('Insufficient Evidence' / INSUFFICIENT_SIGNAL flag), and a repository with a substantive description must produce a gradable, non-abstain verdict. PASS iff abstention tracks the presence of signal. This is the anti-bluffing property: no score is invented from nothing.
gates.D2_page_code_permissions_deterministic: PAGE CODE. Build a CodePermissionTable, run auditChange() over every real repository description, and confirm (a) the audit is deterministic -- identical input yields byte-identical output across two runs -- and (b) an ungranted path is DENIED while a granted path is ALLOWED. PASS iff both.
gates.D3_echo_chain_is_tamper_evident: ECHO DATABASE. Write one record per real repository into EchoDB, compute the merkle root, and verify inclusion for every leaf. Then flip a single character in one record and confirm the recomputed root CHANGES and the stale inclusion proof FAILS. PASS iff all leaves verify before tampering and the tamper is detected.
gates.D4_ei_ledger_verifies: EI. Run EI.evaluate() over the cohort and then EI.verify() on its receipt ledger. PASS iff the ledger verifies and one receipt exists per evaluated repository -- every verdict is accountable after the fact.
gates.D5_agency_allocator_beats_naive: AGENCY. Map the 22 real repositories to allocator nodes (U = log10(stars), D_enc = backlog health, D_dec = fork-through) and run the ConstitutionalAllocator against capacity-greedy and equal-split under an identical budget. PASS iff the constitutional allocator's realized systemic yield is >= both naive baselines. If no repository sits below the collapse floor, triage is NOT APPLICABLE and that is declared as a null, not forced.
gates.D6_replication_reach_is_not_quality: REPLICATION of the surviving finding from PR #111, on a FRESH independent real cohort. Rank the 22 repositories by stars (reputation) and by verified fidelity (license clarity x backlog health). PASS iff the two orderings DIFFER and at least one top-5-by-stars repository falls below the fidelity floor. FALSIFIABLE: if prestige and verified fidelity give the same ordering here, the earlier finding fails to replicate and that must be reported at full force.
gates.D7_license_governance_gap: GOVERNANCE, REAL. Count repositories publishing NO license (SPDX null). Report the exact count and names. This is a descriptive real-world finding about the Qwen/DeepSeek corpus, reported as measured whatever the number -- an unlicensed repository is a genuine downstream-reuse hazard regardless of popularity.
gates.D8_dashboards_render_offline: DELIVERABLE. Three browser dashboards (ASSAY / Page Code / HELM) must be produced as ONE self-contained HTML file with the measured results embedded at build time, containing no external script, style, font or image reference, so it opens from disk with no network and no server. PASS iff the file exists, embeds the run's result values, and contains zero external-resource references.

symmetric_null: Every count and ordering is reported AS-IS. D6 is a genuine replication attempt and MAY fail; a failure to replicate is a valid, reported outcome and will not be retuned. D5 may be declared NOT APPLICABLE if no node is below floor. D7 is purely descriptive -- any count, including zero, is the result. The Hugging Face connector gap is disclosed rather than papered over.
acceptance: GREEN when the spec re-hashes to the manifest, the frozen cohort re-hashes to its pin, and D1-D8 are evaluated exactly as written with any null or non-replication reported at full force. No post-hoc gate changes.
honest_scope: This tests that the stack's components behave as specified on a real, independent corpus, and it ships three offline dashboards. It does NOT evaluate the quality of Qwen or DeepSeek models, does NOT benchmark their capabilities, and makes no claim about which is better. It measures governance-relevant repository telemetry only. Methodology, not speed.
